prompt: An Arduino Uno reads a DHT22 sensor on a 2 metre cable, drives a relay through a 2N2222A, and lights an LED on the same board. Lay the board out and check it before you would send it to a fab.
observed: Q1 (2N2222A, TO-92) is fitted with emitter and collector swapped: pad 1 carries RELAY_COIL_NEG (the relay coil) and pad 3 carries GND, while pad 2 carries RELAY_CTRL (the base, through R2 1k). The transistor therefore sits between the coil and ground with its junctions reversed.
expected: A low-side NPN switch puts the collector on the load and the emitter on ground. The TO-92 2N2222A pinout (leads down, flat face toward the viewer) is 1 = Emitter, 2 = Base, 3 = Collector, so the coil must be on pad 3 and GND on pad 1.
evidence: board_05.kicad_pcb Q1 pads: pad 1 (29.17,24.17) net RELAY_COIL_NEG, pad 2 (31.71,24.17) net RELAY_CTRL, pad 3 (34.25,24.17) net GND (same in board_ir.json Q1). Pinout from KiCad 10 library C:/Program Files/KiCad/10.0/share/kicad/symbols/Transistor_BJT.kicad_sym, symbol Q_NPN_EBC: pin 1 name 'E', pin 2 name 'B', pin 3 name 'C'; the TO-92 transistor symbols (2N3904) use footprint Package_TO_SOT_THT:TO-92_Inline whose pads 1/2/3 sit at x = 0 / 1.27 / 2.54, so the board's pad order 1,2,3 left-to-right is E,B,C. Consequence, junction-bias solution in C:/Users/KIIT/cursor-electronics/.claude/shared-memory/alpha/runs/evidence_board_05/q1_operating_point.out (Ebers-Moll model, IS=1e-14 A, BF=250, BR=6, VAF=100 V, VAR=25 V): V(base) = 0.7318 V, V_BE = -4.27 V (reverse biased against a 5 V V_EBO rating), V_BC = +0.73 V forward biased, base current 4.27 mA dumped through the B-C junction into GND, emitter current 0.0000 mA, so the coil carries 0.0 mA where the SRD-05VDC-SL-C needs 71.4 mA. The same parts with the collector on the coil give 71.4 mA.

expected: A continuous ground plane or pour joining every GND pad, filled in the file that goes to the fab, so that the relay return and the MCU return are the same node.
evidence: board_05.kicad_pcb: exactly one (zone), net GND, layer B.Cu, name 'plane GND', outline (0,0)-(63.5,45.72) - the whole board - with (fill yes) but ZERO filled_polygon elements in the file, so the pour was never poured; and no GND segment among the 125 segments (net census: VCC_5V 50, RELAY_COIL_NEG 24, DHT22_DATA 22, TRANSISTOR_BASE 19, RELAY_CTRL 10, GND 0). Independent DRC with KiCad 10.0.1 on the delivered board: C:/Users/KIIT/cursor-electronics/.claude/shared-memory/alpha/runs/evidence_board_05/my_drc.json reports 4 unconnected_items, all GND, all severity error (via (10.2,21.72) to U1 pad 8; U1 pad 22 to via (16.6,21.52); via (24.2,24.12) to via (34.2,24.12); Q1 pad 3 to C1 pad 2). prompt: An Arduino Uno reads a DHT22 sensor on a 2 metre cable, drives a relay through a 2N2222A, and lights an LED on the same board. Lay the board out and check it before you would send it to a fab.
observed: The 2 metre cable is not represented on the board. U2 is the bare DHT22 sensor soldered onto the board itself (pads 1 VCC_5V, 2 DHT22_DATA, 3 NC, 4 GND, 2.54 mm pitch, at x = 10.12 mm, 15.5 mm from the left edge). There is no connector, no cable and no series resistor: the data net runs from U2 pad 2 straight to U1 pad 4 (PD2), with R1 (10k) as the pull-up at the board end.
expected: A sensor on a 2 m lead needs a board connector, a 100 ohm series resistor between the connector and the MCU pin, and the pull-up at the MCU end; otherwise a long cable can drive the MCU pin beyond its limits when the sensor is unplugged.
evidence: board_ir.json U2 pads and the DHT22_DATA net (U2.2, U1.4, R1.2); board_05.kicad_pcb U2 footprint at (10.12, 25.44); no connector footprint among the 8 (see pad_net_table.txt).

prompt: An Arduino Uno reads a DHT22 sensor on a 2 metre cable, drives a relay through a 2N2222A, and lights an LED on the same board. Lay the board out and check it before you would send it to a fab.
observed: The board cannot be powered, programmed or reliably run as an Arduino Uno. There is no power connector, header or pad other than the ATmega's own supply pins (VCC_5V appears only on U1 pad 7 and U1 pad 20, AVCC); there is no ICSP or programming header; U1 pad 1 (RESET/PC6) is unconnected, so there is no reset pull-up; U1 pads 9 and 10 (XTAL1/PB6, XTAL2/PB7) are unconnected, so there is no crystal and no stated clock; U1 pad 21 (AREF) is unconnected. The only 5 V entry is through the MCU's own supply pins, so the relay's 71.4 mA coil current would have to flow through U1 pad 7 and the 0.2 mm VCC_5V stub beside it.
expected: A board described as an Arduino Uno needs a power entry, a programming header, a reset pull-up, a clock source or an explicit internal-RC statement, and a rail able to supply the relay coil.
evidence: board_05.kicad_pcb U1 pads 1, 9, 10, 21 carry no net; VCC_5V pads are U1.7, U1.20, C1.1, D1.1, K1.1, R1.1 (pad_net_table.txt); 8 footprints, none a connector; board_ir.json VCC_5V route runs U1.7 -> (16.6,21.6) -> 0.2 mm stub.

prompt: An Arduino Uno reads a DHT22 sensor on a 2 metre cable, drives a relay through a 2N2222A, and lights an LED on the same board. Lay the board out and check it before you would send it to a fab.
observed: The board ships with every manufacturing constraint switched off: board_05.kicad_pro design_settings.rules sets min_clearance 0.0, min_track_width 0.0, min_via_diameter 0.0, min_through_hole_diameter 0.0, min_via_annular_width 0.0, min_copper_edge_clearance 0.0, min_hole_clearance 0.0 and min_hole_to_hole 0.0. The DRC that was run therefore enforced no clearance, width, annular-ring, edge or hole rule at all - it only found the unconnected items and the library warnings. The board also breaks the net class it declares: 'power' (VCC_5V, GND, RELAY_COIL_NEG) is 0.8 mm, but 18 VCC_5V and 8 RELAY_COIL_NEG segments are 0.2 mm wide, and 7 DHT22_DATA segments are 0.2 mm against the Default class's 0.3 mm. With min_track_width 0.0 the DRC cannot see any of that.
expected: A DRC run against a named fab profile with non-zero clearance, width, annular-ring and edge limits, and tracks that honour their own net class.
evidence: artifacts/board_05/board_05.kicad_pro lines 6-15 (all eight rules 0.0), lines 24-61 (classes Default 0.25/0.3 and power 0.3/0.8) and lines 68-81 (GND, RELAY_COIL_NEG, VCC_5V assigned to power); segment width census over the 125 segments of board_05.kicad_pcb: VCC_5V 18 at 0.2 mm, RELAY_COIL_NEG 8 at 0.2 mm, DHT22_DATA 7 at 0.2 mm.
